importantNotes: 'Man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart' (16:7).
Saul's disobedience teaches that partial obedience is disobedience.
David's victory over Goliath shows that God uses the unlikely to do great things.
The contrast between Saul (chosen by people's standards) and David (chosen by God).
Hannah's prayer (ch. 2) is echoed in Mary's Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55).

chapters.1: Hannah prays for a son and vows to dedicate him to the LORD; Samuel is born.
chapters.2: Hannah's song of praise; Eli's wicked sons abuse their priestly role.
chapters.3: God calls young Samuel in the night; Samuel's first prophetic message.
chapters.4: The Philistines capture the Ark of the Covenant; Eli and his sons die.
chapters.5: The Ark causes plagues among the Philistines; the idol Dagon falls before it.
chapters.6: The Philistines return the Ark to Israel on a cart pulled by cows.
chapters.7: Samuel leads Israel to repentance and victory over the Philistines at Mizpah.
chapters.8: Israel demands a king to be like other nations; God grants their request.
chapters.9: Saul searches for his father's donkeys and meets Samuel.
chapters.10: Samuel anoints Saul as king; Saul prophesies among the prophets.
chapters.11: Saul rescues Jabesh Gilead from the Ammonites; his kingship is confirmed.
chapters.12: Samuel's farewell address — he warns Israel about the dangers of having a king.
chapters.13: Saul makes an unlawful sacrifice; Samuel rebukes him and prophesies the end of his dynasty.
chapters.14: Jonathan's brave attack on the Philistines; Saul's rash oath nearly costs Jonathan's life.
chapters.15: Saul disobeys God by sparing Agag and the best animals; God rejects him as king.
chapters.16: Samuel anoints David; David plays the harp for the troubled King Saul.
chapters.17: David defeats the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone in the name of the LORD.
chapters.18: David and Jonathan's friendship; Saul becomes jealous and fears David.
chapters.19: Saul tries to kill David; Michal and Jonathan help David escape.
chapters.20: Jonathan and David make a covenant; Jonathan warns David of Saul's murderous intent.
chapters.21: David flees to Nob and eats the consecrated bread; he pretends to be insane before the Philistines.
chapters.22: David gathers followers at the cave of Adullam; Saul massacres the priests at Nob.
chapters.23: David saves Keilah; Saul pursues David in the wilderness; Jonathan encourages David.
chapters.24: David spares Saul's life in a cave at En Gedi — 'I will not harm the LORD's anointed.'
chapters.25: Samuel dies; David, Nabal, and Abigail — wisdom prevents bloodshed.
chapters.26: David spares Saul's life a second time in the wilderness of Ziph.
chapters.27: David takes refuge among the Philistines in the city of Ziklag.
chapters.28: Saul consults the medium at Endor; Samuel's spirit prophesies Saul's death.
chapters.29: The Philistine commanders refuse to let David fight against Israel.
chapters.30: David rescues the captives taken from Ziklag by the Amalekites.
chapters.31: Saul and his sons die in battle against the Philistines on Mount Gilboa.
